title: Everything Else Was Already There
logline: Five machines of 1950 stand in a concrete hall at the bottom of a gorge under four steel pipes that come down the mountain from a pond small enough to walk round, and none of it can do anything at all, in any weather, until water that fell somewhere above has finished arriving.
human_question: If everything needed is already in place and the thing still cannot happen, what exactly is missing?

place.what_kind_of_place: A hydroelectric station of 1950 in a steep wet gorge on the western flank of the central massif, and the chain of water-works strung down the mountain above it. At the top, a small gravity dam about a hundred metres across a stream, holding a pond of only a few hundred thousand cubic metres, fed by a catchment of under twenty square kilometres. From the pond a tunnel driven through rock, then a surge tank on a shoulder, then steel penstocks running down the open slope in parallel lines for the last part of the drop, held on concrete saddles, with a stair beside them. At the bottom, a powerhouse: five machines, three of one size and two of another, the first three brought into service in December 1950 and the last two in December 1958, fifty megawatts in total, under a switchyard and a line of towers going away down the valley. On the next stream over, a fall of a hundred and twenty-six metres. Around all of it, planted slope, forest, cloud that arrives and leaves several times a day, and a road that keeps crossing the pipes.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because it is a condition laid out on a mountainside in the right order, at a scale you can fly along. Water is everywhere here: it is in the cloud, on the road, in the moss on the concrete, in the gorge below. None of that water does any work. Only the water that has been caught, held, taken through a hole in a rock and stood upright in a pipe does work, and the whole installation exists to arrange exactly that one difference. Seen from the air the argument is a drawing: a pond that is doing nothing, a shoulder with a tank on it, four straight lines down a green slope, a flat roof at the bottom with wires going out of it. Seen from inside, the hall is a cathedral of 1950 concrete with five machines in a row and a floor you can feel, and the best minute in it is a machine standing still, with everything in the building complete and ready and a needle at zero. The place also carries its own contrast without any arrangement, because a hundred and twenty-six metre fall on the next stream shows what the same water does when nobody has put it in a pipe.
place.what_moves_or_changes: The pond fills and draws down, and it is small enough that the drawing-down is visible as a line on the concrete. Cloud comes up the gorge and closes the pipes off, then clears. Rain on the catchment arrives at the pond hours later, and the difference is measurable rather than dramatic. The machines start and stop as the system asks for them: a hall that is silent and a hall that is not are entirely different rooms, and the change between them takes less than a minute. Nothing here can be scheduled by the film. Inflow, cloud, and what the machines are asked for that day all belong elsewhere, and the film's one event, a start, happens when it happens.
place.when_it_looks_best: The first hour of light, when the gorge is still holding cloud and the pipes come out of it one at a time; and late afternoon, when the sun is down the valley and the steel goes bright along its top edge. The dry months for flying and for a low pond with its line showing; the first weeks of a monsoon for the fall on the next stream, for the cloud running up the pipes, and for rain on a metal roof over five machines. Inside, the hall has no season and wants a whole day, because the film's argument is the difference between one hour and the next in the same room.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about a beautiful piece of old machinery and the mountain it is bolted to. Cloud moving through a gorge; a small dark pond behind a low dam; a tunnel mouth; a surge tank on a shoulder; four steel pipes going straight down a green slope with a stair beside them; the inside of a 1950 machine hall, its paint, its rails, its dials, its five machines in a row; the floor changing under your feet; water leaving at the bottom and going back into the river; and on the next stream, a hundred and twenty-six metres of the same water falling down a rock face with nothing arranged about it at all. It has a complete shape with nothing said over it, and anyone who likes machinery, or mountains, or the way water behaves when somebody has thought about it very hard, has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same day becomes the detailed method's account of what it means for something to be a support, filmed on the one object where the supports are separated by kilometres and laid out in the order they act. The list is not a way of saying that everything is connected. It is a set of named, bounded powers: helping by having arisen first, helping by still being there, helping from later on, helping by ending and clearing the place, and, the strongest of them, a power so decisive that the book says all the other conditions can be present and nothing will arise without it. A pond, a tunnel, a pipe and a machine are a physical statement of exactly that: every part of the installation can be complete, oiled and manned, and the hall stays silent until a particular condition has come down the mountain. And the voice says out loud what the sources say and the group's own name can make people forget: this is not a picture of a world holding hands. It is a map of which thing holds up which, in which way, and in which direction, and most of these directions run one way only.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high, moving down the mountain with the works: a small dark pond behind a low dam, a shoulder with a tank on it, then four steel pipes in parallel going straight down a green slope into cloud, and at the bottom a flat roof and a switchyard.
sequence.voice: This was finished in 1950. Three machines then, two more in 1958, fifty megawatts between them. The pond up here holds only a few hundred thousand cubic metres, off a catchment of under twenty square kilometres. Everything in this frame exists to make one difference to water that was already falling anyway.

sequence.on_screen: The pond itself at close range. Still, dark, full, silent. The drawdown line on the concrete. Nothing moving on it but rain rings. Then the tunnel intake, and nothing visible happening there either.
sequence.voice: The first kind of help the books name in this part is simply having arisen first. What is already there supports what comes afterwards, they say, as a tree that grew earlier holds up the flowers and the fruit that come later [C082-P:L5723–L5727]. And a second kind is being there at all: things present, in the moment of arising or standing, support other things by their very presence [C082-P:L8230–L8234]. That is all this pond is doing. It is not doing nothing. It is doing the least dramatic of the twenty-four.

sequence.on_screen: The pipes from beside them, walking down the stair. Rivets, saddles, the curve of the steel, moss at the joints. Then a low angle straight up the line of a penstock into cloud, so that neither end is in frame.
sequence.voice: The order cannot be run backwards, and the books are insistent about that. Everything arises leaning on something as a place to stand [C082-P:L3616]; and the leaning is one-way more often than not. The great elements hold up what is derived from them, and what is derived does not hold them up in return; the mind supports the matter it produces, and that matter does not support the mind back [C082-P:L3616–L3620]. Water drives this machinery. The machinery has never once moved the water.

sequence.on_screen: Inside the hall. Five machines in a row, paint, brass, rails, a polished floor. All of it complete, lit, attended, and completely silent. A needle at zero, held.
sequence.voice: And then the strongest of the twenty-four, which is the reason this room can be like this. The book says of it that even when root, object and the other conditions are present, if this particular power is not obtained there is no arising at all [C082-P:L4337]. Nothing is missing from this building. There is no fault, nobody is late, and nothing whatever will happen in here until one condition arrives from four kilometres up the hill.

sequence.on_screen: The change. The hall going from silent to not silent in under a minute: the floor, the air, the dust, the instruments, water going out at the bottom in a heavy grey rope and back into the river.
sequence.voice: What has just arrived is not new water. It is the same water that was in the pond in the first shot, and it did nothing there. The summary of the whole method is six plain relations, and in one of them, where mind and matter support mind and matter, there are nine separate powers doing nine different jobs [C083-M:L5; C083-M:L29; C083-P:L399–L417]. Asking what caused this room to change is the coarse question. The useful one is: in what way, exactly, did each thing help.

sequence.on_screen: The next stream over: a hundred and twenty-six metres of water going off a rock face into forest, with nothing built on it. Then back to the machine hall's tailrace, the same volume, arriving quietly at the bottom of a wall.
sequence.voice: One correction, because a place like this invites the warm version. The list is not a statement that everything is connected. Each condition names exactly which states it supports and, in the first book, which it does not reach [C082-P:L97]. The presence condition in particular is technical and not a moral idea: the same passage that puts the four elements holding each other in place also has delighting in the eye giving rise to lust [C082-P:L8534–L8544; C082-P:L8712–L8722]. And the book says flatly that the unconditioned is not a presence condition at all [C082-P:L8246], so none of this becomes a metaphysics of an all-pervading being.

sequence.on_screen: Evening. The machines coming off load and the hall going quiet again. The pond at dusk, with the drawdown line under water once more. Rain starting high up the catchment, filmed from height, with the station's lights small below.
sequence.voice: The books count ending as a kind of help too. The moment before has to cease for the next one to arise, and if the earlier one had not gone there would be no room for the later [C082-P:L4357]. And support runs the other way in time as well, since what comes afterwards keeps up what was already standing, the way water and weather arriving later keep an already-grown tree alive [C082-P:L6055]. The pond fills at night because the machines stopped.

sequence.on_screen: Last light, back at height. The whole chain in one frame from pond to switchyard, cloud crossing it, the lines going away down the valley. No commentary over the final minute.
sequence.voice: The second book ends the summary with a line that sounds like the slogan and is not. Past, future or present, inside or out, there is no phenomenon that is not a support for something, and everything except two is also supported by something else [C083-M:L31]. That is not a world holding hands. It is an inventory, and its point is that the support runs in specific, nameable, mostly one-way relations, and nobody is running any of them.

concept_merge.why_together: C082 is the only concept in this group that states the film's subject outright. Of decisive support, the strongest of the twenty-four, the first book says that even when root, object and the other conditions are present, if this power is not obtained there is no arising of mind and mental factors at all [C082-P:L4337]: that is a complete machine hall with a needle at zero. Around that one claim the same digest supplies everything else the mountain shows: help by having arisen first, with the tree that holds up the later fruit [C082-P:L5723–L5727]; help by still being there, in the presence condition, which is exactly what a full pond is doing all night [C082-P:L8230–L8234; C082-P:L8534–L8544]; help by ending, since a thing must cease for the next to have room [C082-P:L4357]; help from later on [C082-P:L6055]; the one-way clause, since derived matter does not support the elements it comes from and mind-born matter does not support the mind [C082-P:L3616; C082-P:L3616–L3620]; and the hard limit that nothing arises from a single condition [C082-P:L97]. C083 supplies the summary and the ending: the twenty-four condensed to six relations, with nine distinct powers inside one of them [C083-M:L5; C083-M:L29; C083-P:L399–L417], and the sweeping closing line that nothing is not a support for something while everything except two is also supported [C083-M:L31]. A station that cannot act until one condition has come down a mountain is where those two meet, at a scale a camera can fly along and in an order that cannot be reversed.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That 'the last missing condition' is not a poetic way of saying everything matters. It is a specific claim with a name in the text, and it is visible as the difference between two hours in one room where nothing else changed. The location adds what the page cannot: distance, so the conditions are kilometres apart and arrive in sequence; direction, so the whole chain is plainly one-way; and contrast, because the next stream shows the same water doing nothing of the kind. This idea replaces its previous subject entirely, which was a visiting eye camp with dressings coming off. That film could not be made. It would have put people under medical care on screen at their most exposed, with blindness as its subject and a doctrine laid over an impairment, and a near-identical idea had already been removed from this project for exactly that. The requirement the concept actually needs, something that becomes possible only when the last missing condition arrives, is met here with no patient and nobody's body in it.

concept_links.why: The film is built on one sentence of this digest and filmed inside its consequence. Decisive support is described as the strong cause without which, root and object and the rest notwithstanding, mind and mental factors do not arise [C082-P:L4337]; a hall that is complete, attended and silent is what that sentence looks like, and the film's central beat says so and nothing more. The other named powers are spoken only where the mountain shows them: prenascence at the pond [C082-P:L5723–L5727], presence as the pond continuing to be there [C082-P:L8230–L8234] with the elements holding each other by presence [C082-P:L8534–L8544], reliance and its one-way clause on the penstocks [C082-P:L3616; C082-P:L3616–L3620], postnascence and cessation as help at the end of the day [C082-P:L6055; C082-P:L4357], and the refusal of single causes throughout [C082-P:L97]. Every 'does not transfer' line in this digest that bears on the film is honoured and three are spoken. 'Everything is connected' is contradicted out loud, twice, with the digest's own point that each condition names what it does and does not reach. 'Just being present is a gift' is refused in the same breath as the presence condition is introduced, using the digest's own example of delighting in the eye giving rise to lust [C082-P:L8712–L8722]. 'Presence is universal existence' is refused with the text's statement that the unconditioned is not a presence condition [C082-P:L8246]. 'Letting go makes room for the new' is avoided by giving the cessation clause strictly as the text gives it, one moment ceasing so the next can arise. Nothing here is offered as physics, hydrology or energy science; the film never says the tradition anticipated anything; predominance, repetition, kamma and the grave-act passages are unused; and no person on the site is filmed as an agent of the concept, because the text describes powers and not anyone operating them.

This digest gives the film its middle and its last line. The six relations, and the nine powers inside the one where mind and matter support mind and matter, are named once, at the moment the hall changes, so that the viewer hears a vocabulary rather than a cause [C083-M:L5; C083-M:L29; C083-P:L399–L417]. The closing beat uses the summary's sweeping statement that there is no phenomenon that is not a support for something and that everything except the unconditioned and mere concepts is also supported [C083-M:L31], spoken precisely as the digest frames it, as an inventory of specific relations and not as a slogan. The digest's own limits govern that framing: 'everything is mutually interdependent' is refused in the film's voice, because mutuality is one of twenty-four and many of these relations run one way only, which is also what the penstocks show. The two single-mode relations, matter supporting mind and mind supporting matter, are not used here, since this film has no body in it and borrowing them would be decoration; the digest's flagged editorial reading of the feeling-to-craving joint is not used either. Nothing in this film touches impairment, illness or anybody's faculties, which is the whole reason the idea was moved.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That in this analysis a condition is not a push but a particular manner of helping, that some of those manners are having been there first, still being there, coming afterwards and getting out of the way, and that one of them is strong enough that everything else can be in place and nothing happens without it. And that this is not a picture of universal interconnection: the relations are named, bounded and mostly one-way, and nobody administers them. The station is an analogy and the film says so; no claim is made about anybody's body, circumstances or luck.
what_must_be_real: The installation as it actually is, including what is out of service, leaking, patched, rusted, replaced or noisy. Nothing is repainted, relit, started or stopped for the camera, and no machine is run outside what the operators were going to do anyway. The film accepts that its central event, a start, may not fall inside the window, and does not simulate one. No output, dispatch or grid-condition information is filmed that the operator does not want filmed, and nothing is shown that would matter to the security of a working power station. The people who work there are filmed as people doing work, are not made into characters, are not asked to explain or endorse any doctrine, and are never framed as the ones who make the machines act. No one enters a shaft, a tunnel, a surge tank or a penstock except with the operator's own safety people and on their terms, or not at all.
position_hint: middle to late: it needs a viewer who already accepts that the group is counting kinds of support rather than admiring a web, and it is the group's one statement of the strongest condition, so it sits after the plainer films and before anything that turns back to the chain itself. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Engineering sublime: a 1950 installation in a gorge photographs as heroism, and the film would then be about human achievement, which is the opposite of a text with no agent in it.
Colonial nostalgia, or the argument against it, both of which the site invites and neither of which is this film.
Letting the operators become the ones who make it happen, so that non-agency is contradicted by the footage while the voice asserts it.
Turning the twenty-four conditions into hydrology, or implying the tradition anticipated physics.
Letting 'nothing happens without the last condition' soften into 'everything is connected', which is the group's standing error and is refused twice in this film's voice.
Making the presence condition sound like a moral idea about showing up, which the digest explicitly forbids.
Dam-and-power politics: water allocation, tariffs and outages are live public arguments here and are not this film's subject.
Filming anything that compromises the security or safe operation of a working station, or pressing for access to a confined space for the sake of a shot.
Building the film's climax on a start-up that then has to be arranged, which would make the one honest event in it a staged one.
drop_if: The operator will not permit the machine hall to be filmed, since the difference between a silent hall and a running one is the film's centre.
No start or stop falls inside the filming window and the only way to have one is to ask for it.
Height cannot be flown over the works at all, so the chain from pond to powerhouse cannot be seen as one thing.
Access to the pond, the surge tank or the penstocks is refused, leaving only an interior, which is the concept with its order removed.

connections.note: Two films about a machine and its conditions: one where everything is present and one thing is missing, one where everything is present and several small things have quietly failed.
Two chains of support laid out in order and running one way: one over months in a planted bed, one over four kilometres of mountain in an afternoon.

selection.reason: It replaces an unmakeable idea with the same requirement met on a machine instead of a patient, and the one image the place produces, a complete and silent hall waiting on something four kilometres away, is the strongest of the twenty-four conditions stated exactly.

review.note: Rewritten 2026-09-24, and the entire subject was dropped rather than adjusted. What was dropped: a visiting cataract camp, in which dressings came off one by one on a single morning and each patient found out what they could now see, with some not improving. That film cannot be made on this slate. It would have filmed people under medical care at their most exposed, with blindness as its subject and a piece of doctrine laid over an impairment; the patients carrying the idea could not meaningfully consent to that use of a surgical outcome; several digests in this series forbid letting doctrine touch a real person's impairment; and a near-identical idea had already been removed from this project for the same reason, which the old record itself noted as a duplicate. Nothing of it is kept: no camp, no patient, no faculty, no eye, and no body of any kind. What was kept is the requirement underneath it, that something becomes possible only when the last missing condition arrives. That requirement now has a name from the sources rather than a medical event: decisive support, of which the first book says that all the other conditions may be present and nothing will arise without it. The concept links were re-chosen accordingly. C075 was dropped, because its place in the old idea was the eye among the twenty-two faculties and that material is exactly what must not be brought near a person's sight. C083 was retested and kept, for the summary of the six relations and for the closing line that nothing fails to be a support for something. C082 was added as primary and carries the film. Both digests were read from scratch and every citation tested against digest evidence; nothing was carried over from the old text.

suggested_location.name: The Old Laxapana power station and its penstocks below Norton Bridge

also_known_as.name: Norton Bridge power station
also_known_as.meaning: the older name for the same station, after the settlement at the dam above it

also_known_as.name: Laxapana
also_known_as.meaning: read locally as laksha pahana, a hundred thousand lamps, the name given to the falls on the neighbouring stream and then to the stations

also_known_as.name: penstock
also_known_as.meaning: the steel pipe that takes water from the tunnel down the last of the fall to the machines

suggested_location.region: Nuwara Eliya District, Central Province: the Ambagamuwa hill country on the western flank of the central massif, in the gorge of the Kehelgamu stream a few kilometres above where it joins the Maskeliya stream to form the Kelani
suggested_location.why_here: Because the concept is the installation's physical layout. Every condition the film needs is a separate object, kilometres from the next, arranged in an order that cannot be reversed: a small gravity dam about a hundred metres long holding only a few hundred thousand cubic metres off a catchment of under twenty square kilometres; a tunnel through rock; a surge tank; steel penstocks down an open slope; and a 1950 machine hall three and a half kilometres downstream with five units in it, three of eight and a third megawatts and two of twelve and a half, the first three commissioned in December 1950 and the last two in December 1958. That gives the film the one image it exists for, a complete and attended hall in which nothing will happen until one condition has come down the mountain, and it gives it at a scale a camera can fly the whole length of. The gorge also supplies the contrast for nothing: on the next stream there is a hundred and twenty-six metre fall of the same water with nothing built on it at all. And because the works are strung down an open slope rather than buried, the single most beautiful shot the place produces, four straight steel lines down a green mountain from a pond to a roof, is also the clearest statement of an ordered, one-way chain of conditions.
what_to_film: The whole chain from height in one move at first light: pond, tunnel line, surge tank, penstocks, powerhouse, switchyard, with cloud crossing it.
The pond at close range, still and doing nothing, with the drawdown line on the concrete and rain rings on the surface.
The intake and the tunnel mouth, held long, with no visible event at all.
The penstocks from beside and from directly below: rivets, saddles, moss at the joints, the line going up into cloud with neither end in frame.
The machine hall complete and silent, with the instruments at rest, held far longer than is comfortable.
The change from silent to running, in one take, with the floor, the air and the dust in frame rather than the people.
The tailrace: water leaving at the bottom of the wall and going back into the river.
The fall on the neighbouring stream, in the same week, filmed plainly and without drama.
The works as they actually are: patched concrete, replaced sections, leaks, a machine out of service, a stair that has been repaired many times.
Cloud arriving and taking the whole installation away, and the moment it comes back.
suggested_location.access: By road into the hill country from the west and then on the estate and station roads that cross the pipes; the works belong to the national electricity utility and nothing here happens without its written permission, which is a serious ask for a working station of national significance. The machine hall, the switchyard, the dam, the surge tank and the penstock line are all separately controlled, and a crew would have to fit the station's own operating day, not the other way round. Confined spaces, the tunnel and any climbing on the penstocks are out unless the operator's own safety people run it. Drone flight over a power station and its switchyard needs specific clearance and may simply be refused; the gorge is also steep, wet and prone to cloud that closes visibility in minutes. Access on foot to the fall on the next stream is a separate matter again and is a walk.
suggested_location.best_time: The dry months for flying, for a low pond with its line showing and for hard light on steel; the first weeks of a monsoon for the fall on the neighbouring stream, for cloud running up the pipes and for rain on the powerhouse roof. Within a day, the first hour and the late afternoon for the works outdoors, and a full working day inside the hall, since the film's argument is the difference between two hours in the same room.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only and unverified on the ground. From the sources above: the dam above the station is a gravity dam about a hundred and three metres long across the Kehelgamu stream, begun in 1924 and operational in December 1950, impounding a reservoir of about 390,000 cubic metres with a surface area of 0.15 square kilometres off a catchment of 19.4 square kilometres; water goes from it through a rock tunnel and steel penstocks to the station three point eight kilometres downstream; the station has five units, three rated at 8.33 megawatts and two at 12.5, totalling fifty megawatts, with the first three commissioned in December 1950 and the last two in December 1958, and is operated by the national electricity utility; its published position is the one given here; the fall on the neighbouring stream, which the stations are named after, is a hundred and twenty-six metres on the Maskeliya stream and is recorded as being in this district, while the dam itself is described in the sources as being in the province rather than by district. Several things this film depends on are inferences rather than confirmed facts about this station: that the machines are started and stopped rather than run flat, that the pond's drawdown is visible as a line, that the hall is as quiet when idle and as physical when running as the film assumes, and that the works are visible along their whole length from the air. The flow of the neighbouring fall is affected by diversions in the same system, and the film does not claim to know how much. Nobody has been approached and no permission has been sought from the utility or from any authority whose clearance aerial work would need. No photograph of the station, the dam, the surge tank or the penstocks was found on Wikimedia Commons; the one image is of the fall on the next stream.

unknowns: Whether a working station of this significance can be filmed at all, and who inside the utility has to agree.
Whether a start or a stop can be observed inside the window, since the film refuses to ask for one and the whole centre of it is that change.
How the units are actually operated: whether the hall is ever genuinely silent and complete, or whether at least one machine is always running.
Whether drone flight is possible over a power station, its switchyard and its transmission lines, or whether the chain has to be filmed from the road and the slope.
Whether the dam, the surge tank and the penstock line can be reached and filmed, since the film's order depends on all three.
Whether the site's politics, its 1920s to 1950s history and the current arguments about power supply can be kept out of a film that is about none of them.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
